title: How Databases Work: SQL vs NoSQL in 60 Seconds 🗄️ #shorts
description:
Every like, message and order is saved in a database. SQL databases store data in tables with a strict structure and are queried with SQL; NoSQL databases store documents, key-value pairs or graphs with flexible structure. When to use each, plus how indexes make lookups instant.

lines: Every like, every message, every order you place gets saved somewhere.
That somewhere is a database, built to save, find, and update data, fast.
SQL databases store data in tables, like a super-powered spreadsheet: rows, columns, and a strict structure.
You ask questions in SQL. Select name, from users, where city is Chennai. Answer: in milliseconds.
NoSQL databases are more flexible. They store documents, key-value pairs, or graphs, with no fixed structure.
Use SQL when data must stay consistent, like bank transactions. Use NoSQL for flexible data at huge scale, like social feeds.
And an index works like a book's index: the database jumps straight to your data, instead of reading everything.
SQL for structure. NoSQL for flexibility.
